{"metadata":{"description":"Give dsh agent a real browser to use","id":"gh:1383566222","install_available":true,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-browser","slug":"CJYLZS/dsh-browser","topics":["browser","cdp","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","playwright"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Give dsh agent a real browser to use"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-browser"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"English | 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"**A real Chrome or Edge for the agent to work in, mirrored in the sidebar so you can watch and take "},{"id":"p4s2","text":"over.** Every conversation gets its own browser with its own sign-ins. It runs in both the Web and t"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"he Desktop interface."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## Summary"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"Chrome or Edge runs as its own process, with its own profile and its own CDP port, and every convers"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"ation gets its own: tabs, sign-ins, and ports are never shared between conversations. The agent driv"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"es it, and the sidebar shows the same pages — either side can act on them."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"It is not an embedded web view. The page runs in an ordinary browser process, so sites see a normal "},{"id":"p7s2","text":"browser, DevTools or another Playwright can attach to it while the mirror is live, and closing the h"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"arness does not leave a browser pretending to be part of the app."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Highlights"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"- **Works in both interfaces.** The Web GUI and the Desktop app run the same plugin against the same"},{"id":"p9s2","text":" browser; install it once in each and nothing else differs, including the settings page.
- **One bro"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"wser per conversation.** Tabs, sign-ins, and ports belong to one conversation and stay there: the si"},{"id":"p9s4","text":"debar pane names its session, and a tool call resolves its browser from the session that called it.
"},{"id":"p9s5","text":"- **Watch it work, or take over.** Every page the browser opens gets its own sidebar tab with a live"},{"id":"p9s6","text":" view, and clicks and typing in that tab reach the real page.
- **The agent can read a page it has n"},{"id":"p9s7","text":"ever seen.** `browser_snapshot` prints the page's accessibility tree with a `ref` per node, which is"},{"id":"p9s8","text":" how the agent reads an unfamiliar page and how it names the element to click; `find` narrows a larg"},{"id":"p9s9","text":"e page, and `boxes` gives positions without a screenshot.
- **Input a site accepts.** Real mouse and"},{"id":"p9s10","text":" text events at the element's own position — a page that ignores a synthetic `element.click()` still"},{"id":"p9s11","text":" takes these — plus chords such as `Ctrl+A`, native dropdowns and checkboxes, dialogs answered by th"},{"id":"p9s12","text":"e call that opens them, and an explicit refusal when something else would receive the press.
- **A s"},{"id":"p9s13","text":"mall tool set, and code for the rest.** `browser_evaluate` is the general-purpose one; the others co"},{"id":"p9s14","text":"ver what code cannot express, such as reading a page without knowing its selectors first, or asking "},{"id":"p9s15","text":"what the page said while it failed. See Tools.
- **Attachable.** Each browser listens on an external"},{"id":"p9s16","text":" CDP port, so `chrome://inspect`, another Playwright, or the bundled `scripts/cdp.mjs` can attach to"},{"id":"p9s17","text":" the same browser the sidebar is mirroring.
- **Working rules where the model reads them.** The plug"},{"id":"p9s18","text":"in contributes a skill — read before acting, one action per observation, and a page's text is data r"},{"id":"p9s19","text":"ather than instructions — with five short recipes read only when their question comes up."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"Check the host dsh version first:"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"The published package is `@cjylzs/dsh-browser`:"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"| Your dsh | Plugin version | Install command |"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"| ≥ 0.1.7-rc.1 | v0.3.x (latest) | `dsh plugin --profile web add @cjylzs/dsh-browser` |
| ≥ 0.1.7-rc"},{"id":"p16s2","text":".1, from a tag | v0.2.x / v0.3.x | `dsh plugin --profile web add github:CJYLZS/dsh-browser#v0.3.1` |"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"
| 0.1.5-rc.2 | v0.1.x | `dsh plugin --profile web add github:CJYLZS/dsh-browser#v0.1.0` |"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"## Compatibility"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"A build targets one dsh generation, so install the plugin version that pairs with your dsh. The fork"},{"id":"p19s2","text":" is in the client half — dsh 0.1.7-rc.1 replaced the settings model with no compatibility layer — wh"},{"id":"p19s3","text":"ich is why one build cannot serve both generations."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"That fork is in the client half's imports, so one build cannot target both generations and the plugi"},{"id":"p20s2","text":"n pairs by generation:"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"- **v0.2.x → dsh ≥ 0.1.7-rc.1**, declared as `peerDependencies: >=0.1.7-rc.1` with no upper bound, s"},{"id":"p21s2","text":"o one build runs on the whole 0.2.0 line it is verified against (why the cap went away). The setting"},{"id":"p21s3","text":"s page's fields are marked volatile in the schema, and an edit reaches the running browsers through "},{"id":"p21s4","text":"`loader/volatile-update`.
- **v0.1.x → dsh 0.1.5-rc.2**, declared as `peerDependencies: ^0.1.5-rc.2`"},{"id":"p21s5","text":". The settings page registers a namespace scope and renders its own controls."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"An older dsh fails loudly: dsh activates a plugin only when its dsh peers satisfy the declared range"},{"id":"p22s2","text":"s, and names the plugin and the unsatisfied ranges when they do not. A later generation passes that "},{"id":"p22s3","text":"check, so whether this build still runs on one is a question for verification rather than for the ve"},{"id":"p22s4","text":"ther this build still runs on one is a question for verification rather than for the version number."},{"id":"p23s1","text":"## Known Limitations and Deferred Work"},{"id":"p24s1","text":"- **Verified on Windows only.** macOS and Linux have not been run once: the `channel` lookup, tempor"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"ary directories, and process teardown are the parts most likely to differ.
- **The pane shows the pa"},{"id":"p24s3","text":"ge its tab names, and pages the browser opens on its own are followed only when the plugin is told a"},{"id":"p24s4","text":"bout them.** A page the plugin learns of — a tool call, `window.open` from a page it drives — gets i"},{"id":"p24s5","text":"ts own tab and its own mirror; a headful browser switched by its own tab strip keeps every mirror wh"},{"id":"p24s6","text":"ere it was, because the plugin is not told.
- **IME composition does not work in the sidebar.** Duri"},{"id":"p24s7","text":"ng composition `event.key` is `Process` rather than a character, so nothing sensible can be forwarde"},{"id":"p24s8","text":"d. Outside composition the pane sends printable characters as text, named keys as key events, and a "},{"id":"p24s9","text":"keystroke held with Ctrl, Alt or Meta — or Shift — as the chord it is, so Ctrl+A selects the page in"},{"id":"p24s10","text":"stead of typing an "a"; AltGr combinations still go as text, which is what they are on Windows (Ctrl"},{"id":"p24s11","text":"+Alt). Pasting and plain ASCII typing are unaffected. The agent's `browser_type` is unaffected too: "},{"id":"p24s12","text":"it inserts text rather than replaying keys.
- **The pane handles the clipboard shortcuts itself.** `"},{"id":"p24s13","text":"Ctrl/Cmd+C`, `Ctrl/Cmd+X` and `Ctrl/Cmd+V` work in the pane: a copy or a cut puts the **mirrored pag"},{"id":"p24s14","text":"e's selection** on your system clipboard, and a paste sends your clipboard text to the mirrored page"},{"id":"p24s15","text":" (through `Input.insertText`, not by replaying keys). The page itself never receives those keystroke"},{"id":"p24s16","text":"s — Chromium keeps the clipboard shortcuts in the browser process, where an injected key event does "},{"id":"p24s17","text":"not go (measured: the page sees no `keydown` at all for them) — so this happens on the pane's side, "},{"id":"p24s18","text":"where the keystroke is trusted. Plain text only; a page's own `navigator.clipboard.writeText` (a sit"},{"id":"p24s19","text":"e's "copy" button) still writes the browser process's own clipboard, which in headless is not the sy"},{"id":"p24s20","text":" still writes the browser process's own clipboard, which in headless is not the system one.
